supplied_claim_assessments.claim: modernc.org/sqlite is a CGo-free port of SQLite generated from C with ccgo.
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: The database/sql driver is CGo-free and vendors platform-specific Go generated from SQLite C sources. ccgo generation reduces manual porting, but modernc.org/libc and generated platform code remain material dependencies whose exact versions and behavior must be tested.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: It cross-compiles to Android and iOS out of the box with ordinary GOOS/GOARCH settings.
supplied_claim_assessments.assessment: partly demonstrated, not a support claim
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: The pinned version built an Android/arm64 executable with CGO disabled and a c-shared library with the NDK, but upstream does not list Android or iOS as supported. No Android runtime was available; iOS requires external linking and could not be built or run on this Linux host.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: It is only slightly slower than C SQLite and the difference is negligible for mobile.
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: The maintainer benchmark is workload-dependent: modernc was roughly 3.2-4.8 times slower in representative large insert tests while often faster in repeated or concurrent reads. It uses older driver versions, DELETE/FULL rather than Notrios WAL/FTS5, and only two averaged runs; H0 needs a Notrios-specific emulator benchmark.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: It stays exactly in sync with upstream SQLite.
supplied_claim_assessments.assessment: tracks upstream closely, exact parity is not guaranteed
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: v1.57.0 reports SQLite 3.53.3, but the modernc changelog also carries a pre-upstream journal-recovery patch and records generated-code and ABI fixes. Version alignment and automated translation do not replace behavioral validation.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: Database files are 100 percent byte-for-byte compatible with C SQLite.
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: SQLite-format interoperability is the relevant property; independent executions are not required to produce byte-identical files. A Linux C-to-modernc-to-C WAL/FTS5/JSON round trip passed integrity_check, but Notrios still requires bidirectional desktop/mobile schema-v27, checkpoint, snapshot, restore, search, and sync tests.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: FTS5 is included without a separate extension.
supplied_claim_assessments.assessment: verified on the supported Linux probe
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: v1.57.0 reported ENABLE_FTS5 and executed an FTS5 create/insert/MATCH probe. Every selected target must still record compile_options and run the real Notrios migration/search suite.

supplied_claim_assessments.claim: The driver runs the official SQLite suite and therefore perfectly matches upstream semantics.
supplied_claim_assessments.correction: The project documents builders and extensive target tests, but no test suite proves perfect equivalence. Notrios must validate its own failure, concurrency, backup, FTS5, and recovery contract.

android_arm64.reason_runtime_not_executed: zero connected Android devices and zero configured AVDs
android_arm64.conclusion: promising build feasibility only; not Android runtime support

ios_arm64.ordinary_cgo_disabled_build: failed because Go ios/arm64 requires external linking
ios_arm64.conclusion: unverified; requires a macOS/Xcode/gomobile or equivalent host gate

desktop_cross_builds.conclusion: viable H0 desktop candidate on upstream-supported targets

browser_js_wasm.failure_boundary: modernc.org/libc platform packages have no selected js/wasm files
browser_js_wasm.conclusion: not a Flutter Web SQLite adapter

sequence: C created a WAL database, ordinary table, FTS5 table, JSON query, and checkpoint
modernc opened it, read and wrote FTS5 content, ran JSON, used WAL, and returned integrity_check=ok
C reopened it, read both engines' content, ran JSON, checkpointed, and returned integrity_check=ok
linux_file_interoperability_probe.scope_limit: Linux format interoperability only; not byte identity or mobile/desktop Notrios compatibility

performance_reference.author_warning: Do not trust benchmarks, write your own; the run is not very scientific.
performance_reference.notrios_conclusion: No universal faster/slower claim is justified; measure WAL, FTS5 indexing/search, migrations, snapshot/restore, sync, package size, RSS, latency, and sustained writes on the selected emulator ABI.

architecture_decision.jetpack_canonical_owner_redesign: rejected unless separately approved as a whole-store redesign
architecture_decision.android_h0: A/B the pinned C amalgamation control against pinned modernc.org/sqlite; modernc is a promising build-only candidate, not selected.
architecture_decision.desktop_h0: Keep the existing C store while running the same A/B. Adopt modernc across supported desktop targets only if semantics, file interoperability, failure behavior, size, RSS, and Notrios workload performance pass.
architecture_decision.flutter_web: Do not use modernc.org/sqlite v1.57.0. Keep Web over REST, or plan a separate browser-local SQLite/Wasm/OPFS adapter and ownership contract.
architecture_decision.single_owner_rule: Only one SQLite engine may open the canonical database in a process; Flutter/Jetpack and Go must never concurrently own the same file.

blocking_h0_gates: pin exact modernc.org/sqlite and exact modernc.org/libc versions, licenses, checksums, provenance, update cadence, and generated compile options
run the modernc Android c-shared library on the selected emulator API/ABI and record sqlite_version plus compile_options
run the pinned C amalgamation control on the same emulator, settings, storage path, and test corpus
execute schema-v27 bootstrap/migrations, CRUD, WAL/checkpoint/crash recovery, FTS5 indexing/search, JSON, snapshot/restore, and synchronization for both candidates
round-trip checkpointed production-shaped databases C-to-modernc-to-C and desktop-to-Android-to-desktop with integrity and FTS5 checks
benchmark representative initial import, sustained writes, repeated/concurrent reads, FTS5 search/indexing, archive snapshot/restore, and sync rather than relying on the maintainer benchmark
measure per-ABI APK/AAB and library size, build time, cold start, latency distribution, CPU, allocation, and peak RSS
validate database/sql connection, busy/locking, cancellation, error-code, DSN, backup, and failure semantics against the current direct C wrapper
prove one SQLite engine owns the canonical file and no Flutter/Jetpack or platform SQLite connection can open it concurrently
run iOS only on a supported macOS/Xcode host and keep it post-1.0 until that gate passes
